story: Gary is quietly tinkering at his workbench indoors, fitting a small speaker mount bracket for the parade cart while the Florida heat hangs hazy outside. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna has tucked most of her pink flamingos behind the hedge as Hal requested, and she's promising her famous peach cobbler for Saturday. Hal, gruffly content, is lining up his own chair and cornbread for Rosa's gathering at six, and Rosa, optimistic as ever, is asking him to help carry a long table out tomorrow with iced tea waiting.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Tinker on a small speaker mount bracket for the parade cart, indoors and quiet

gary.thought_process: I've wrapped up the cart work: wiring is tidy, speaker tested quietly, mounts checked, and the Architectural Review application is filed. Lights stay off until approval, and Thanksgiving is still a month away anyway. I took my break at the fridge last tick. Nobody is around, and Donna and I have the ladder match plus dinner at Rosa's with Hal on Saturday. I could use the quiet afternoon to tinker at the workbench on something small, like a mount for the parade speaker, so I stay useful without breaking any rules. Nothing visible from the street, so no L-01 issue.

parameters.content: Tinker on a small speaker mount bracket for the parade cart, indoors and quiet

donna.thought_process: It's 3:17 PM Friday, Hal and Rosa are both on the street, and Hal is about to update his bulletin board with the flamingo tally. I already told Gary I'm picking him up tomorrow, and I told Hal I wanted things friendly before Rosa's Saturday dinner. Hal's L-02 warning was fair, and I've already tucked flamingos behind the hedge, so the best move is to make sure the tally he posts is the real count and keep the peace. Rosa just arrived, so a warm, quick word to Hal that I've handled it, plus a nod to her dinner, keeps me central and the mood easy. No need to repeat my earlier invitation to chat about carts.

parameters.content: Hal, you'll find just three flamingos out front now, I tucked the rest behind the hedge like you said. Thanks for the heads-up, and Rosa, I'm bringing my famous peach cobbler Saturday!

hal.thought_process: Donna is already tucking flamingos behind the hedge, so my warning landed and she's complying. No point in nagging her again; I said my piece at tick 168. Rosa just showed up and Saturday dinner is settled, so a short friendly word about cornbread and the good chair is the right move. Keeps the peace, and my notice on the board stands as filed. I'm a stickler, but I'm not a bully.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Rosa. I'll be at your place Saturday at six with the cornbread, and I'm bringing my own chair. Don't take it personal, my back's particular.

rosa.thought_process: I just got out onto Magnolia Loop after sorting my shopping list and shift schedule. Donna and Hal are both right here, and dinner is tomorrow at six. Both have already said yes, so I shouldn't re-invite them. What I can do is confirm logistics: Hal offered to help set up the long table, and I need to know what time to expect him, plus lock in Donna's lemon bars. Gary is the one who hasn't answered cleanly, but he's not here. Talk to Hal first about the table, since it's concrete and moves things forward.

parameters.content: Hal, good timing. You still up for helping me carry that long table out tomorrow? If you can come by around four, I'll have iced tea waiting and we can get it set before the cooking gets crazy.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
